examples.solution_text:
(a) The vertical midline is a line of symmetry: folding along it puts the left half exactly on the right half. Folding along $AC$ does not make the halves match.
(b) The horizontal midline is also a fold line. There are $2$ lines of symmetry.

examples.question_text:
This is a non-square rhombus.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75,every node/.style={font=\normalsize,text=black}]
\draw[black] (0,-1.6)--(2.9,0)--(0,1.6)--(-2.9,0)--cycle;
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
(a) Does it match its starting position after each turn about its centre: $90^{\circ}$, $180^{\circ}$, $270^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$?
(b) State its rotational order and identify its lines of symmetry.
examples.solution_text:
(a) No, yes, no, yes. A half-turn puts each vertex on the opposite vertex. A quarter-turn does not match the longer and shorter diagonals.
(b) It matches twice during one full turn, so its rotational order is $2$. Its two diagonals are its $2$ lines of symmetry.

examples.question_text:
This general parallelogram is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75,every node/.style={font=\normalsize,text=black}]
\draw[black] (0,0)--(4.5,0)--(5.8,2.2)--(1.3,2.2)--cycle;
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
(a) State the number of lines of symmetry.
(b) State the order of rotational symmetry.
examples.solution_text:
(a) No fold makes the halves match, so there are $0$ lines of symmetry.
(b) A $180^{\circ}$ turn maps the parallelogram onto itself. It matches twice during one full turn, so its rotational order is $2$.

New content uses Stage 3 fold-and-turn reasoning, editable TikZ, black diagram ink and unshaded shapes. Final rendered label-size verification remains for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: The rhombus vertices are (-2.4,0), (0,1.3), (2.4,0) and (0,-1.3). Reflection across AC swaps B and D; reflection across BD swaps A and C. EF and GH pass through the centre but neither reflection preserves the vertex set. Therefore only AC and BD are symmetry axes. The solution diagram shows exactly these axes. This adapts the supplied fold test and candidate-line exercise within Stage 3 scope.

The bottom and top sides are horizontal, with lengths 4.6 and 3.0. The sloping sides have direction vectors (0.4,1.8) and (-1.2,1.8), so they are not parallel. Their squared lengths are 3.40 and 4.68. The unequal bases cannot be exchanged by reflection; an axis preserving both would have to pass through their midpoints, whose x-coordinates differ: 2.3 and 1.9. Hence the drawing has exactly one pair of parallel sides and no symmetry axes. The matching arrow marks correctly identify the parallel sides. This directly adapts source question 5(b).
